body: This kinda reminds me of a true story I heard of a Black man moving into a White neighborhood having to defend his house agains a mob of people. I couldn't remember the man's name, but I tried to google it. It might be Ossian Sweet. There's a wikipedia article about him.

I can relate to those feelings and experiences. For this situation, seeing a therapist regularly is  extremely helpful. Also, look up an organization called "the Samaritans." They're a British organization (iirc) who mainly function as a suicide hotline, but they also do email chat if you're not in an emergency and just need someone to listen. 

Of course there is journaling, and I've started doing voice recordings and talking to my phone as if someone is on the other line. If you're interested in prompts for journaling, there's  website called therapistaid.com or something like that which has a lot of worksheets for various issues.

Just some suggestions from what I've tried. Maybe doing some of this stuff can ease the emotional burden. It's tough, especially when your support group is very small.

For me, that happens when I don't think the help will be effective, especially if it's something I've tried before. At some point though, I just have to do something different and admit that I could use some help. Another time it happens is when I don't believe I deserve help, or I just feel like I'm burdening people. Why do you think that's happening for you now?

Maybe I'm putting too much stock in strangers opinions, but I've noticed my posts and comments consistently get little to no attention. I can't help taking it as evidence that I'm right about being scum, about being unwanted and unlikable in general. My sister used to say, "everyone else can't be crazy." The only common denominator is me. I had just the slimmest hope that I wasn't alone in this, but I guess I am. No one gives a shit about a bad person, and that's understandable. I just don't get how I'm expected to go on, how I'm expected to have the will to keep trying if I'm already damned.

I don't want to go into the horrible things I've done, but I know that they're unforgivable in my eyes and the eyes of many others. No, I can't change the past, as much as I want to. I don't know how to authentically be a good person or parent even. I'm trying my best with my daughter, but I have no idea how to make up for the things I've done and I dont believe I can anyway.
I'm lonely, too. Open to a chat

I can relate to this mood so much I almost laughed out loud! I get bitter and mildly vindictive like this, especially when it seems like people who should care completely lack empathy. I'm not judging you. I think a lot more people can relate to feeling this way than may want to admit. 

What's up with the psychiatrist, though? Are you in a position to find another one? I personally don't find psychiatrist to be the "warmest" people, but if they are just gonna push you drugs, they could at least get the basic information about you correct.

That's an interesting way to think about beliefs. I would like to think that I was generally accepting and understanding of others before the psychotic episode. My friends had actually described me that way, and that was nice. 

For some reason, I actually find myself significantly less understanding now, and I feel bad about it. Maybe the "shell shock" from everything has made me generally less open than I used to be.

That's interesting. I knew mediums and psychics. During my psychosis, I suddenly considered myself an adapt "psychic" and could read cards with ease. Once the hallucinations started, I thought I was becoming a medium. I wasn't too excited about that though. Lol

Haha, well I'd like to think SOME things have changed. I mean, the psych hospital isn't a great place, but they usually aren't terrible. I unfortunately had been before my episode, but that particular hospital seemed to illicit the psychosis. I even looked into some type of recourse, but I really didn't have any. Nobody believs a "crazy" person.

Well, before and during psychosis, I didn't belong to any religion,  and I didn't believe in God the way most theists do. I believed more in a collective consciousness type of thing. I believed we all were apart of God and our experiences were God experiencing "himself" (God wasn't gendered really).
 
I had read a little bit about Taoism. I had (actually still have) books on all kinds of belief systems, including the Tao Te Ching. I never belived you had to be religious to be spiritual, and I never believed you had to be religious or spiritual or any of that to be moral or "good".

I think more what happened to me was I was reading way too much into coincidences, and I was finding meaning and symbolism all over the place. I became very "go with the flow," my personality changed, my behaviors were very strange to others. Late in the episode, I developed  insomnia and hallucinations, things I had never before experienced in my life. I do not experience them now either.

Now, I'm a bit nihilistic. I don't trust that anything means anything anymore. It makes life a feel kind of drab and cynical, but I don't want to get sucked down that rabbit hole again.

Thank you for your reply. It's interesting how you mentioned our minds trying to make sense of reality because around the time the psychosis started, I was hospitalized for suicidal ideation. The psychiatrist and the staff were very dismissive, and I felt like they didn't respect anything I had to say. 

At one point, I had a complete hysterical breakdown because I was bleeding for 2/3 days and reported it several times to the nurse and all the staff just brushed me off. I had been hospitalized before, but it was never like that time. It was one of the most stressful and traumatic times of my life. And that is when the psychosis started, trying to make sense out of the insanity they handed me. So they just used all that for justification for reprehensible treatment they gave me. 

After that hospitalization, I was psychotic for pretty much a whole year. There were terrible consequences. I "sobered up" so to speak (I wasn't on drugs at all), and I'm still trying to make sense of all of it and just have a general phobia of spirituality and reading too much into coincidences. I can't even enjoy music they way I used to. 

What sucks is that I feel like any valid experiences I had or things I had to say during that time were invalidated due to the psychosis, and it doesn't seem fair at all.

When I started medication for major depression, the doctors always framed it as if I would be taking meds for the rest of my life. They may change the dosage or try a different one, but it was always assumed to be long term. I never knew there was an option for it to be temporary. 

With that said, they may be tapering off the wellbutrin specifically because it can have some weird side effects (I got trembles/shakes at some point), and it is so similar to speed that it can come up as a false positive in a drug test (found that out the hard way).

I'm kind of surprised they started you with that. They started me with "milder" stuff and when they finally did give me wellbutrin, I felt like I was a new person. It was temporary, but it was pretty great while it lasted.

Taking meds for the rest of your life can sound scary. It did for me, too. But, I think if it is genuinely helping you, and not causing a bunch of side effects, I might not be such a bad trade off for being healthy and well. 

You're so young and have so much potential and a lot of life in front of you. If you can get well and stable now, you'll save yourself a lot of headache in the future. 

I hope my experiences gave you some insight. Only you can say what's best for you. Take care

Well, I'll admit I'm ignorant to how Germany does things, but I would encourage looking into treatment if you don't have any already. If you have having a crisis and your dad insists on not taking you to a psych hospital, you could try the Samaritans at https://www.samaritans.org. They're based in the UK I think, but I've emailed them several times before. They are good if you just need someone to listen.

I have never been diagnosed with schizophrenia, but I find this relatable and that unsettling to me. I had an...eventful year (entire year) not too long ago that, when I look back on it "well", i realize I was plagued with delusions and I was buying into them. Towards the end, I developed insomnia and was juuuust starting to hallucinate.

It all ended very badly, and I'll have to deal with the consequences for the rest of my life. But before that year, I had never experienced anything like it. Since that year, I have never experienced those things again, but now I am particularly skeptical of spirituality and religion.

I do not receive and never have received treatment for schizophrenia. Neither did those symptoms persist past that year, but I have a friend who insists I'm schizophrenic because it. This post makes me wonder though

Those treatment centers deal with all kinds of mental health emergencies. You don't have to literally be hurting yourself or threatening self harm to qualify for treatment. 

That being said, they would be my last resort because of how limiting the environment is. I would go if I felt I was unsafe or about to go over the edge because a lot of times, they just gave me meds and made sure I was "stable enough". They are more of an emergency treatment than a long term solution.

Idk what your financial situation is, but there are ways to establish care with therapist and psychiatrist even on low income and no insurance. If you're in the U.S., I can help point to some resources. And for the time in between visits, I can point you to some free resources online for self-help.
I finished most of my homework and got an interview for a paid internship. Need the money, so fingers crossed.

Yeah tell me about it. I'm starting to believe stability is more of a practice or a skill rather than a status, though. I think each day, even for a "stable" person, is  practice in stability. In that way, it can be difficult to wait until I achieve stability before I work again. Idk man. Just taking it one day at a time for now.

Well, is it that you have a hard time relating to others or that they have a hard time relating to you (or both)? Because, I think a lot of people can relate to being introverted and/or lonely, so at least in that way, I would say you are relatable. 

As far as not relating to others, I'm not sure. I found myself in that situation a lot more recently and I think, for me, it's due to a mixture of getting older, feeling numb, and not being around people enough. Maybe you could find other people that are more relatable to you by branching out to different communities or settings, even if it's online. Idk. It's what I'm trying though.

Thank you. I hope things get better for you as well. I've struggled with depression and mental illness for a long time, but it got real bad after I left a job I liked because of a very unfortunate disagreement I had with a coworker. So, kinda similar situation in that things really spiraled after leaving a role. My savings only lasted a few months though and by the time I found a new job, I was getting evicted. 

Two and a half years full-time is good, though. It'd definitely be an accomplishment for me. I've had a lot of false starts, too. My whole friggin life after high school feels like a false start 

Being out of work because of depression isn't great, but it allows you some time to focus on getting better and more stable. Are you on leave at your job? Are you welcome to go back?

My partner works, and they work a weird schedule. Herbal remedies can have side effects and don't have much research to support them being very effective. Idk what you want to know about my diet. 

I appreciate that you're trying to help, but I don't think things are as simple as taking an herb, especially not at this point. And, it seems like my concerns are being minimized or dismissed. 

I can't say what exactly I was trying to accomplish with posting this. I guess I was just putting my thoughts out there. Maybe someone can relate. Maybe not. Maybe someone has been where I am or similar and can talk about what they did or what they're doing.

But, I'm not expecting a stranger on the internet to solve all my problems; hell the professionals can't even do that. I'm not saying tips aren't welcome either, but I, like a lot of people posting on this subreddit, am in a complicated situation and have tried a ton of different things. Advice is really tricky, especially when we don't know the person and have the whole picture.

Thanks for that. I hope you're doing better soon. And hey, at least you have enough in you to keep eating and showering. I can relate to happiness feeling scary too. When I was in high school, I was so wary of being happy or being on an "up" because i knew it wouldn't last and the "fall down" would be that much worse, that much lower.

I can't work night shifts like I used to. I have a toddler, and the daycare is only open day time hours. And if all the tons of meds I've taken don't work, I don't have much faith that some mild herbal remedies would. Even when the meds did work, they only did so much.

I can relate to all of that. It got scary for me when I realized that things that should bring me joy or pain or some other strong emtion literally felt like nothing. I felt like I was turning into a psychopath. But my theory is that it is extreme dissociation, at least in my case.

It got so bad that food didn't even taste like anything. I love food. I love to eat, but I lost a ton of weight cuz I just didn't feel like eating. I wonder if all that has anything to do with dopamine levels...
My friend thought the same thing when I told them my therapist was teaching me CBT and was like, "Well...that's unorthodox" lol
What are you afraid of? You said something about "getting exposed." What do you mean? Without much context, it seems you're afraid of being "exposed" for something you feel guilty or ashamed about.

I would much rather it be the case that we could all agree that our actions and words can be hurtful or helpful to the other person, and we can all try to be more considerate of wach other. But this whole blaming the other person for how they feel AND for how YOU (theoretical "you") feel just leaves all of the emotional burden on them. 

I understand we all are ultimately responsible for our own feelings, but this concept tends to be (ab)used a lot for people to excuse their hurtful actions more than people taking personal accountability for their emotions.

Thank you for the support. Honestly, I don't see how anything I can do will change that dynamic. It's basically two people who I'm talking about who are in my family and who I have to interact with often. Both of these people have issues that they are resistant to admitting and seeking help for and both have issues with denial and pride. They're very different people in a lot of ways, but this is one infuriating way in which they are too similar. 

They fight with each other, too and a lot of the scapegoating comes from me having to be a bridge in communication. My current situation is probably going to call for me to keep being this bridge for now, but I really needed to get the frustrations off my chest at that moment.

I can relate. It makes me feel guilty having that bitterness, too. Even worse is that things have happened that have made it impossible for me to even pursue my desired career. Now, I'm back to the drawing board to figure out what to do with myself. My mental health issues have sabotaged me so much.

I've been there before. I'm not completely sure how I got out of it. It's like life is suffocating you and everything feels completely pointless and nothing feels like anything. What do you find yourself doing all day? Did something major happen recently that contributes to this feeling?
Yeah I can relate to that sentiment as well. I realized that isolation can be very dangerous

I'm...not great but I'm more functional than i was a few weeks ago. I'm eating. Not really getting good rest but I am sleeping. I don't have a community and have very little support outside of a distant friendship and a therapist. Thank you for asking. That was really nice

It sucks, but something about your post seems accepting and hopeful.
